claims.statement: Conformance is differential: each Workers/DO program runs on identical bytes, once on workerd and once on celld, and the two outputs must be equal — proving the program is real Cloudflare code and celld honors the contract simultaneously; the corpus only grows, ported from workerd itself including the Durable Objects contract, web-platform globals, and WPT, with pre-release binary replays in each deployment mode.

The coordination protocol is specified in TLA+ (written against celld v0.1.0 by Heyang Zhou); model checking found four real bugs plus a split-brain that lost an acknowledged write, none of which surfaced in review or testing; most configurations carry pinned failing verdicts because each failing configuration models a past bug or broken checker and must keep producing its counterexample so the model cannot silently lose its tooth.

The model grants the implementation a linearizable object store and perfect shared clocks, and checks exactly the promises of one-writer-per-epoch and no-lost-acknowledged-write — including the argument that a stale owner's late writes cannot cost an acknowledged write because the epoch in the key keeps its lineage apart.

Model checking removed shipped code: celld once sealed a cell's durable history at restore but the verdicts showed the seal defended only a never-acknowledged write (which celld does not promise against) and its permanent cut could turn a recoverable slip into permanent loss, so the seal is gone; the specs are a hand-synced snapshot deliberately not run in CI (a silently stale gate is worse than none) with a delta ledger for model-vs-code gaps.

Deterministic simulation drives the pure decision core's on_event interface (no I/O of its own), so the simulator injects latency, CAS races, lost responses, clock drift, and per-await crashes while V8 stays out because it is not deterministic; each run is seeded so a failure replays identically, properties check safety (two writers per epoch, lost acknowledged write, expired-lease resurrection) and liveness (armed alarms fire, ownership settles), properties must survive tens of thousands of seeds, and the checkers themselves are tested against deliberately broken variants.

The live fleet lab covers what simulation cannot see (S3 tail latency, kernel behavior, V8 under memory pressure): rotating workloads with per-cell checksums, archived evidence bundles, and fault injection between verification passes — SIGKILL mid-write-stream with local-db deletion (all acknowledged writes return), frozen owner whose moved lease makes it refuse old state with exactly-once cross-node writes, node cut off from the bucket (self-fences), an injected 429-throttled bucket (slows to store rate without amplifying), and full-host stops with cells moving and rejoining without duplicate residency; across all runs no acknowledged write was lost and no committed state was damaged.

Trusted numbers carry their measurement conditions: 5,500 claim attempts by 500 concurrent claimants yielded one writer per epoch with zero violations; warm resident requests do zero bucket operations at ~1.1ms p50/~7ms p99; a lab fleet measured ~600ms bucket proof vs ~25ms fleet proof with the bucket race and shared uploads; ten 4-vCPU/8GB nodes held 10,000 resident cells and 20,000 WebSockets with ~11s tail restore after losing two nodes; the page also records the failure edge — a fleet at its resident limit without headroom degrades under multi-node failure.

The conformance/simulation harness wires into the shipped lib.rs under a celld_internal_tests cfg with an env-driven include seam (contract/world/O3-oracle/sim-store/cell-host modules), deliberately excluded from the public build so shipped and harness builds keep the real asyncrt; the release image's test stage depends on cargo test and clippy passing.
